mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 0.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.25% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% indicates a contraction in real economic activity, reducing corporate earnings expectations and resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of GDPC1 YoY < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of UNRATE > 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average by more than -3% for three consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, reducing corporate revenue prospects and causing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12M MA by > -3% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of INDPRO weakness as defined.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST below their respective 6-month moving averages signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which depresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 6M MA and HOUST < 6M MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST fall below their 6M MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% in a single month, combined with stable FEDFUNDS, signals inflation surprise without policy response, eroding real corporate earnings and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during months of CPIAUCSL > 3% with stable FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average by more than +1% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12M MA by > +1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained above-average payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 and RSAFS above their 12-month moving averages by more than +2% signals a broad-based demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12M MA by > +2% AND RSAFS > 12M MA by > +2% simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS exceed their 12M MA by > +2%.
